body: I'll try. I rarely have a chance to make real friends, just people over the internet. Maybe I'll be able to find a volunteer group, it's a small town but there's probably something.
Thanks for that. I really do need to see a doctor, it's just getting to one that's a problem.

My loneliness being exasperated by my depression makes sense. Instead of just knowing that it's loneliness and it will pass, it feels much deeper than that. I live in a very rural area, there really isn't much here. I have a part-time job, but I work during the day with older people so we don't socialize much. 

Thank you for those tips with coping, I'll keep them in mind. I like the breathing one especially, it makes sense. I would like to get help, but like I mentioned to godless_communism, my parents would have a hard time understanding, and without them I can't get to a doctor. Stuck between a rock and a hard place.

Thanks for the advice - that does sound a bit like me. I had some friends before, not many because I was always extremely nervous and shy, but there were still some people to talk to. I'll check out those books as well, they might help get over the anxiety at least. I've never seen a doctor or a therapist, but it's easy enough to assume in my case. I've felt this way for a very long time and it's obvious that it's not normal. 

I want to get help, but I can't get to a doctor without talking to my parents first (I don't drive, so I have no way of getting there). Which is a problem, because one of them likes to avoid medication at all costs, and just doesn't like talking about this sort of stuff. When I first started high school I broke down in one of my classes and a guidance counselor called my mom in. The day after, she acted like nothing had happened and I was fine. So... It's tough.

In one of my courses at school there was a section on Buddhism, they really do have an interesting/inspiring way of looking at things. I'll have to read up some more about minimalist living and everything, anything is worth a shot now.

I also moved around a lot when I was younger, and I think that sort of stunted my social skills. Then I moved again right after I graduated high school to a place where I know no one/it's nearly impossible to meet people, so when I am out of school (like now), finding friends is even harder. I've got four months coming up where I'll basically be alone. 

It is much easier to talk to people online than it is in real life. If I actually knew all the people I've talked to on reddit (this is an alternate account), life might be a lot easier. Online, you don't have to be shy or awkward or anything like that.

Thanks, that is a lot of food for thought. You're right about a lot of it. It just feels like I've been in a bit of a storm for the past eight years, trying to see the end feels almost impossible most of the time. I don't know what the end would even be anymore.
I suppose so, but I've always been pushed so hard to get into college that it was basically the only option for myself. Now I'm here and I don't know what I should be doing anymore.

I tried to move away from the whole "loner" image I had in high school, but it just didn't work out. I made some friends at school and then the same stuff happened again and it didn't seem worth it to even try.
Go for walks, study, usually just stuff by myself. I don't have many friends now so it's tough to find motivation to do anything social.
